summary.title: ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU

setting_and_object.category: System (action-conditioned interactive video world model + deployment stack)

details: Interactive world modeling couples four bottlenecks that scaling a video model alone does not solve: action-supervised data, a unified control interface, long-horizon autoregressive drift, and real-time deployment on practical hardware.
Few-step distillation alone does not yield an interactive system; latency, throughput and VRAM must be optimized jointly.

ABot-World-0: an action-conditioned video world model driven solely by raw keyboard inputs (8 discrete keys, additively injected at patch embedding) covering both first-person scene roaming and third-person character control, plus reference-character memory tokens (negative temporal RoPE, asymmetric attention) for identity persistence.

Training crux: a bidirectional action-conditioned teacher is progressively converted into a causal few-step student via teacher forcing and causal ODE distillation, then LongForcing — a final distribution-matching (DMD) stage that supervises long student self-rollouts with an extended-horizon teacher to counter accumulated distribution shift.

Systems crux: a co-designed streaming inference stack (lightweight VAE decoder, low-bit DiT, efficient attention, bounded KV cache, memory-aware module scheduling) targeting single-desktop-GPU real-time rollout.
5B model fine-tuned (full-parameter) from the pretrained Wan2.2 video DiT backbone.

Per-frame 8-dim multi-hot keyboard vector (W/A/S/D movement, I/J/K/L rotation); 4 frames packed into 32-dim tokens to match VAE temporal patch size, mapped by a camera-adapter-style module (PixelUnshuffle + conv + residual blocks) and added to patchified latent tokens.
Reference-character identity: 4 directional person crops plus a synthesized canonical frontal portrait, VAE-encoded and prepended as memory tokens.
Chunk-wise causal generation: 3 latent frames per chunk = 12 decoded frames.

Three sources: AAA games (largest, ground-truth controls via runtime API, 1920x1080, first- and third-person), simulation (Unreal Engine plus ABot-3DGS reconstructions of proprietary aerial/street-scan assets), and internet video (driving, walking tours, aerial) with pose-estimated pseudo-action labels via displacement projection and thresholding.

WorldExplorer agent-driven collection: navigation agent over navmeshes, millisecond-synchronized multimodal capture (<33 ms cross-modal error at 30 FPS), task templates, and a training-feedback loop (weakness diagnosis -> collection-ratio adaptation with coverage floors).

Quality control: 14 deterministic checks over six dimensions in three stages plus VLM screening; VLM captions deliberately omit camera motion and are prefixed with a game identifier token; semantic tags for stratified sampling.
Single NVIDIA RTX 5090, batch 1, 1280x704 (720P); action-to-first-frame latency defined as keypress until first decoded frame of the chunk is available.

Components: SageAttention2 attention backend, LightVAE (pruned TAEHV-inspired decoder), FP8 / MXFP6 / MXFP4 quantization of DiT linear layers (VAE and text encoder kept higher precision), Fast-RoPE (local-window re-anchoring + Triton kernel), FramePack-style module swapping, bounded local-context KV cache with rolling eviction (plus explored KV quantization).

WorldRoamBench sub-dimensions: strict/partial action accuracy, trajectory score, aesthetic and imaging quality, physical mechanics, memory; baselines Genie 3, HappyOyster, LingBot-World (14B), HY-World 1.5 (8.3B).

LongForcing ablation: adapted Causal-Forcing-style baseline (same self-rollout histories and final DMD, shorter-horizon teacher) over 60-second rollouts, measured framewise by HPSv3, high-saturation pixel ratio, perceptual blur, patch repeat ratio.
Qualitative stress tests: hour-scale and day-scale rollouts, out-of-domain scene/character control, physical-interaction cases (collisions, snow footprints, water traces, wall blocking).
System ablation table over incremental optimization variants reporting DiT/VAE time per chunk, FPS, and peak VRAM.

key_findings.finding: Real-time 720P interactive rollout on one consumer GPU requires full-stack co-design, not a single faster operator.
key_findings.evidence: The base pipeline and the SageAttention2-only variant both OOM at 1280x704 on an RTX 5090; adding LightVAE gives the first feasible point (9.12 FPS, 20.49 GiB), FP8 DiT cuts chunk DiT time 1191.1 -> 845.2 ms (12.41 FPS, 15.93 GiB), +Fast-RoPE 786.9 ms (13.27 FPS), and MXFP4 reaches 638.8 ms / 15.83 FPS at 17.15 GiB; the reported envelope is up to 16 FPS with 1.2 s action-to-first-frame latency and <=19.3 GiB peak VRAM.

key_findings.finding: LongForcing (extended-horizon teacher supervision over long student self-rollouts) reduces autoregressive visual drift beyond the training horizon.
key_findings.evidence: Over 60-second rollouts, the Causal-Forcing-style baseline shows progressively decreasing HPSv3 with rising high-saturation pixel ratio, perceptual blur, and patch repeat ratio in the second half, whereas LongForcing keeps higher HPSv3 and lower values on all three artifact metrics; the gap widens with rollout length.

key_findings.finding: A single 5B model with a raw-keyboard action interface is competitive with much larger or proprietary interactive world models on controllability and visual quality, while lagging on temporal memory.
key_findings.evidence: WorldRoamBench: ABot-World-0 (5B) scores 0.5266 strict / 0.7290 partial action accuracy, 0.6752 trajectory, 0.5039 aesthetic, 0.4651 imaging, 0.5223 mechanics — second-best on most sub-dimensions behind HappyOyster and ahead of Genie 3 on action accuracy, and far above LingBot-World (14B, e.g. 0.3235 strict) and HY-World 1.5 (8.3B, 0.1640); memory score 0.5041 trails Genie 3 (0.6073) and HappyOyster (0.6309).

key_findings.finding: The unified keyboard action space transfers to unseen scene-character combinations and yields emergent physical responses not encoded in action labels.
key_findings.evidence: Out-of-domain rollouts with both environment and controllable subject outside the training distribution produce action-consistent character motion coherent with the scene; physical-interaction cases show box pushing, temporally consistent water disturbance, persistent snow footprints, and wall/railing blocking without interpenetration, despite no symbolic physics or collision annotations in training.

key_findings.finding: Hour- and day-scale rollouts remain coherent rather than collapsing, indicating stateful rather than clip-wise dynamics.
key_findings.evidence: Timestamped keyframe strips from five hour-scale rollouts and four day-scale stress-test rollouts retain recognizable scene structure, viewpoint consistency, actor identity, and active motion at sampled checkpoints, without observable collapse into static frames, texture noise, or repetitive content.
